newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Russian crude flows to Czechs, Slovaks on Druzhba.
newsitem.headline: Russian crude flows to Czechs, Slovaks on Druzhba.

text.p: Russian crude was flowing into the Czech and Slovak republics on Thursday, breaking a pattern of new year interruptions on the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline, local oil industry officials said.
Oil flows were halted to east European customers in January the past two years after Russia refused to pay increases in Ukrainian transit tariffs.
Russia in both cases finally agreed to new rates.
"There are no interruptions in the supplies of Russian oil, as for today," Ales Soukup, the spokesman for the primary Czech refiner Ceska Rafinerska a.s. told Reuters.
A dispatcher upstream at the Slovak state-owned pipeline operator Transpetrol told Reuters that crude was flowing normally at mid-afternoon on Thursday.

Soukup said that the 1996 start-up of the Ingosltadt pipeline, delivering Middle East crude to the Czech Republic from a terminal on the Transalpine link in southern Germany, made the Czechs much less dependent on Russian crude.
"Even if there was a break, there is Ingolstadt and we also have enough reserves," Soukup said.
